advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Make a carried-forward divergence declaration record/compare the declared parameter-diff shape so a changed divergence on an already-declared tool re-fails until re-justified.
evidence: merge_declarations: `prior = (previous_tools.get(name) or {}).get("divergence")` then `entry["divergence"] = dict(prior) if ... _declared_reason(...) else {"kind": "undeclared", "reason": ""}` — carried forward for any still-diverging tool regardless of whether the divergence shape changed
_check_divergences appends UNDECLARED only when `not declared` and STALE only when surfaces agree; it never compares the current divergence to the declared one

test docstring test_a_declared_divergence_still_fails_once_the_real_shape_moves: 'declaring a divergence pins the SHAPE it was declared for' — but that test only reddens via _check_descriptors (manifest != live), which cannot fire in the real --check flow because --update regenerates descriptors from live
advisory.finding: merge_declarations() carries a prior `divergence` reason forward onto an already-diverging tool without checking that the divergence SHAPE is unchanged, so a real change to that tool's parameter divergence is absorbed by the stale reason once the manifest is regenerated with --update. The test docstring claims a waiver 'pins the SHAPE it was declared for', but evaluate() only checks whether ANY divergence currently exists plus whether a reason is present (_check_divergences), not whether the divergence matches a declared shape; in the --check flow the descriptors always match because --update rewrote them. So an existing exact/co_names divergence that grows or loses a parameter still passes.
scenarios: A human writes a reason for edit_ticket's enumerated-field divergence; later a new editable field is added to the enumeration and the maintainer runs --update; the reason carries forward and --check stays green, defeating the manifest comment 'a new editable library field must be added here too'
